strategy.intro: Platformization of the CO-NEWBIZ new-business review assets — per-module marketability analysis, licensing policy review, and a build-vs-outsource sourcing strategy on Target Pricing.
strategy.recommendationBody: Keep the stage orchestration and RAG scoring engine in-house as the platform core; take the proxy-chain core open source to claim the ecosystem while monetizing data connectors — a hybrid licensing strategy. Limit outsourcing to non-differentiating areas (UI/charts/reporting) and isolate regulatory-data risk behind subscription external APIs.
strategy.mod1Desc: A 6-stage flow (Screening → Pre-FS → FS → DD → entity IC → group IC) with enforced Kill Criteria. Directly portable to other new-business evaluation processes.
strategy.mod1Pricing: Offered to external affiliates/PEFs as SaaS licenses or embedded on-prem
strategy.mod2Desc: Six-dimension grading (green/amber/red; finance, market, data-trust, regulatory, technology, risk) priority rules plus a data-confidence cap. Regulatory-framework independent.
strategy.mod2Pricing: Usage-based billing per assessment or annual license
strategy.mod3Desc: Antitrust HHI, certification transferability, incentive clawback, debt contingent-liability simulation — a package of 6 required validators.
strategy.mod3Pricing: Flat module subscription, cheaper than deal-size-linked success fees
strategy.mod4Desc: Demand estimation chain for industries lacking direct market data (confidence grades A/B/C). Automated public-statistics and upstream linkage.
strategy.mod4Pricing: Core MIT-licensed; data connectors and calibration paid
strategy.mod5Desc: Seed-fixed reproducible NPV/P50/P95 and contingent-liability probability distribution integration. Independent of the financial modeling toolchain.
strategy.mod6Desc: Why-it-matters based term governance, interpretation Q&A registry, ADR index. Turns organizational knowledge into an asset.
strategy.mod6Pricing: Embedded in platform royalties; no separate sales
strategy.pillarPlatformPt1: 34 agents + the MCP REST-only layer separated into independent modules
strategy.pillarPlatformPt2: Dual core (orchestration·RAG) vs add-on (industry·region profiles) structure for extensibility
strategy.pillarPlatformPt3: Multi-tenant isolation: per-project membership·MNPI·audit logs on shared platform infrastructure
strategy.pillarPlatformPt4: Packaging boundary designed for white-label deployment to external affiliates/PEFs
strategy.pillarMarketabilityPt1: Orchestration·RAG engine: the largest new-business evaluation demand (High)
strategy.pillarMarketabilityPt2: M&A DD·Monte Carlo: targets the deal advisory market (Medium-High)
strategy.pillarMarketabilityPt3: Proxy chain·glossary: ecosystem lock-in effect (Medium / Low)
strategy.pillarMarketabilityPt4: Investment priority by marketability grade: 2 core → 3 add-ons → 1 asset
strategy.pillarLicensingPt1: Two core modules: commercial SaaS/embedded licenses (IP defense first)
strategy.pillarLicensingPt2: Proxy-chain core: MIT open source to claim the ecosystem, then paid connectors
strategy.pillarLicensingPt3: Monte Carlo: PyPI + enterprise SLA support contracts
strategy.pillarLicensingPt4: Glossary/governance: non-sale internal assets, embedded in platform royalties
strategy.pillarPricingPt1: In-house cost basis: labor + infrastructure + regulatory data subscriptions
strategy.pillarPricingPt2: Outsourcing baseline: keep in-house if equivalent quotes exceed 70% of in-house cost
strategy.pillarPricingPt3: Module pricing: a mix of deal-size/assessment-count usage billing and annual flat licenses
strategy.pillarPricingPt4: Penetration pricing: free for affiliates first, then staged monetization for external PEFs

agents.intro: Ask the PM agent. The PM classifies your query, assigns the best-fit agent (or agent chain), and consolidates each agent''s perspective into a proposal. Every response is proposal-only; final judgement and recording belong to humans. Linking an opportunity also hands its evidence (factors, scores, verdicts) to the agents.

onboarding.heading: Get started
onboarding.objective: Four steps to your first new-business review — AI drafts each stage, and a human records every decision.
onboarding.s1Desc: Search and pick a market (industry) or register a new one by KSIC code, then run the 8-step analysis.
onboarding.s2Desc: Discover opportunities in the analyzed market and rate attractiveness with evidence-based opportunity and risk factors.
onboarding.s3Desc: Evaluate synergy with group/affiliate capabilities and strategic fit, then select opportunities.
onboarding.s4Desc: Decide Greenfield (own capabilities) vs Brownfield (partnership and investment) — later stages guide you from there.
onboarding.promotionDesc: After completing S5 (greenfield) or S7 (brownfield), promoting to a project opens S8–S12.
onboarding.projectStagesDesc: S8 business case → S9 due diligence → S10 investment structure → S11 investment review and execution → S12 post-investment — a human gate decision records each transition.
